tagline: Stops AI-generated documentation from becoming false memory.
one_line: Doc Governor repairs the documents code changes affect, then decides which documents an AI coding agent is allowed to believe.
description:
## The problem
Coding agents can turn outdated documentation into confident mistakes. Solo developers repeatedly ask agents to update documentation, yet repairs, verification, and later reads remain disconnected.

## What Doc Governor does
Doc Governor connects three moments: before commit, during pull-request review, and whenever a coding agent requests a document through MCP.

A deterministic Git dependency scan identifies affected documents. A read-only Strands Repair Planner on Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Nova Lite) inspects only its assigned document and changed declared dependencies. It returns a bounded plan. A configured coding-agent executor edits allowed documents in an isolated repository; verification and source/index integrity checks must pass before publication.

A separate read-only coding-agent session checks explicitly delegated contract documents against sources, tests, and deployment evidence where relevant. Repair is not approval. The coordinator requires a completed model session, matching snapshot, valid citations, and no unresolved claims. It records a hash-bound receipt and append-only ledger entry. This review remains a model judgement, not a mathematical proof of prose truth.

PR governance retains deterministic findings and conflict checks. Exact still-authorized coding-review receipts avoid redundant semantic auditing; changed evidence or revoked authorization invalidates them. Other documents retain their existing review policy. The optional Strands governance graph uses narrow Evidence Auditor, Conflict Resolver, and Contract Drafter roles.

The read-only MCP server checks stored usability, document and dependency hashes, and delegated review authorization. A refused get_document response contains no document body and supplies source pointers when available. It does not prevent a client from using other filesystem tools.

## Real use: Firstgram staging maintenance
Firstgram used this workflow for an additive nonunique B-tree index on avatar-upload ticket user_id. Real Strands planning and program-driven Codex execution changed database documentation prose. Independent review caught an incomplete inventory command and an imprecise permission description; both were corrected before trust was recorded.

The index was applied only to staging. Captured evidence confirms a valid/ready index, disappearance of the specific missing-index Advisor finding, and unchanged access restrictions. This is not a measured query-speed improvement or production deployment. Firstgram PR #16 and Doc Governor PR #1 passed their checks and were merged. Firstgram is a private integration repository; judges can use the public generic fixture without its source or credentials.

## Why Professional Agents
The agent takes repetitive documentation maintenance out of a developer's commit-and-review routine and prevents invalidated context from being supplied through the governed read path. Its distinctive boundary is that repairing a document and trusting it are separate decisions.

## Testing and limits
The final integration source passed 220 tests and 24 subtests. The public deterministic fixture runs without AWS. Real Bedrock execution requires the operator's own short-lived AWS credentials and access to the configured model. Mocked tests and configuration flags are not proof of model execution. The catalog is owner-maintained; drift checks cover Advisor output, not complete environments. Stored TTL is not recomputed on every MCP read.

## Reproduce
Install from the public repository following README.md, run python scripts/demo.py, and optionally use --mcp-stdio with the MCP extra. Architecture and testing instructions are included. No private Firstgram source, credentials, or production data are required.
source_disclosure: Doc Governor began as a deterministic iteration in the public SophieYu04/doc-governor repository; this submission builds on that work rather than claiming every component was independently rewritten. Git history retained in the submitted repository records development beginning September 5, 2026. Strands planning/governance, isolated coding-agent repair, independent trust receipts, MCP enforcement, and AWS integration are included in the submitted history. Firstgram, a separate pre-existing private application, supplied the maintenance problem and staging integration case; its application is not submitted as new hackathon work. Standard Python, Strands, AWS, MCP, GitHub tooling and AI coding assistants were used. Eligibility is determined by the organizers; commit dates alone do not establish originality.
